extracted.intended_audience: members, ministers, elders, and readers concerned with the Reformed (Covenanted) Presbyterian Testimony and church polity
extracted.subtask_description: A denominational testimony and supplementary memorial that sets out standards for judging fidelity to the Covenanted Reformation: what constitutes faithful church government, ministerial conduct, terms of communion, and civic behaviour for members in the United States and British contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use of ecclesiastical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Church courts must not 'depose and cast out of the communion' persons who never submitted to their authority, nor 'debar and excommunicate from the holy sacrament of the supper' those only because they cannot conscientiously acknowledge the authority of usurpers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline is abused when applied to persons outside legitimate jurisdiction or used to punish refusal to acknowledge unlawful authorities; such conduct is termed 'tyrannical power over the heritage of the Lord.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful constitution of church courts
rubrics_metrics.description: A court (Presbytery/Synod) must be 'lawful and rightly constituted' according to Scripture and the testimony of the true Presbyterian Covenanted Church; bodies claiming parity of power without such constitution are not rightful courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bodies styled 'Associate Presbytery' or 'Synod' that claim parity of power but lack conformity to the Word and historic covenanted testimony should not be countenanced or submitted to in their authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification required for separation or claiming judicial authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who break off communion or 'presume, in a judicial capacity, to threaten church censure' must allege substantive reasons grounded in the standards of the Reformed Church; mere refusal to approve a condemned point of doctrine is insufficient ground for threatening censure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unwarrantable separation and presumptuous threats of censure without proper grounds are condemned; refer to published vindications for particulars of such errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to ordination vows and scriptural boundaries of communion
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers must not adopt 'a loose and latitudinarian scheme of principles' that tends to 'destroy the scriptural boundaries' of church communion or contradict their ordination vows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sermons or writings (e.g., 'Bigotry Disclaimed') advocating latitudinarianism are cited as examples of principles inconsistent with faithful ministry and likely to lead people into error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union agreements must address prior errors explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts or terms of union must explicitly address and require recantation of prior lax practices (e.g., occasional hearing, communicating with the Revolution Church, public praying for Erastian government) rather than glossing them over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'smooth closing of the wound' without probing practical applications is insufficient; unions published without addressing these items are judged inconsistent with faithfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of occasional or indiscriminate hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of occasional or indiscriminate hearing, and ministerial intercommunion, is condemned as evidence of unsteadfastness and tending toward catholic (open) communion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law of the church on hearing must be maintained; habitual occasional hearing is cited repeatedly as a sign of declension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to British covenants and public/social covenanting
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominations and members should recognize the civil part of the British covenants as binding; public, social covenanting (national or ecclesiastical) is a permanent duty founded on the moral law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open denial of the obligation of the British covenants, ridicule of covenanting, or renouncing the civil parts is singled out as evidence of unfaithfulness to covenant obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic conduct consistent with covenantal loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should not cooperate to maintain 'national rebellion against the Lord and his Anointed' (e.g., giving suffrages to known enemies of Immanuel, serving on juries in ways contrary to the covenant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in civic acts that amount to recognizing or supporting unscriptural civil governments (including voting for ungodly candidates or adopting naturalization/oaths inconsistent with covenant duty) is criticized as disloyalty to the covenant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural warrant required for forming or dissolving ecclesiastical organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Founding or dissolving church organizations (e.g., the Associate Reformed Church) must be warranted by Scripture and not be 'a breach without a definite object' that multiplies divisions needlessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizing a new body while inviting others to dissolve their organizations is criticized as imposing a new term of communion that forces conscience-violations and is tantamount to 'unmitigated tyranny.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of fixed-vs-occasional communion distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel distinction between 'fixed' and 'occasional' communion is unsound and practically tends to catholic communion and eventual merger with other bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction is treated as a practical experiment that undermines strict terms of communion and facilitates the absorption of ministry/membership into the General Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct doctrine of the magistrate 'circa sacra'
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctrine concerning the civil magistrate's authority in sacred matters must be sound; denying the magistrate's role 'circa sacra' leads to errors about Christian duty in civil life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controversies over the magistrate's power are cited as causing breaches of organic fellowship; unsound positions have led to secessions and practical apostasy in civil conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of boundless toleration incompatible with Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: Church polity should not adopt 'a boundless toleration' modeled on republican civil constitutions or assign to conscience a sphere incompatible with subjection to the Scriptures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a secular term like 'Constitution' for an ecclesiastical symbol is viewed as militating against Scripture's supremacy; conformity to civil toleration models is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve authoritative rules of society and worship
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not supplant venerable 'Rules of Society' with ambiguous 'Guides to Social Worship' that lack formal sanction; authoritative regulations should not be displaced by spurious or equivocal productions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republishing ambiguous guides under Synod's recommendation without formal sanction is criticized as preparing for doctrinal and practical declension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent and decisive judicial responses by governing courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Synod and other judicatories must give clear, non-equivocal rulings (e.g., on occasional hearing); ambiguous replies or procedural evasions (laying on the table, 'returned') are signs of weakness or corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to hear petitions, 'laying on the table,' or using technicalities to dismiss grievances are cited as contributing to schism and decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not to expunge historic covenanted standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Historic documents and deeds (e.g., the Auchensaugh Covenant) should not be expunged from the church's symbols; doing so evidences accommodation to the world and departure from reformation principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expunging such deeds (as in 1822) produced secession and is presented as an 'outrage upon the constitution of the Reformed Presbyterian Church.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of uniting with voluntary, multi-professional associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniting with or inducing members to fellowship in voluntary, irresponsible associations 'composed of persons of all religious professions and of no profession' is condemned as unwarranted by Scripture and subordinate standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble resolution: such association is condemned; the court ought to inquire into and address these practices as sins of omission and commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of Synod to investigate and call for repentance
rubrics_metrics.description: When society is agitated, Synod has the duty 'to know the signs of the times,' to 'inquire' into grounds of God's controversy with the church, and to require confession, mourning, and forsaking of sins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proper procedural response is investigation, public confession, and renewal of engagement so 'the Lord may return'—failure to do so (e.g., laying such papers on the table) is censured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of minority protest and separation when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If legal and judicial means fail to reclaim a backsliding majority, a virtuous minority may have the duty to assume an independent position to practically carry out their testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical precedent: formation of a Presbytery in Alleghany (June 24, 1840) by minority adhering to reformation attainments is presented as the correct remedy for irreclaimable majorities.
